content.comment_body: Due to an error on my part, I accidentally applied 230V to the 24V DC input. Although the CPU doesn't show visible external damage, the internal fuse has blown. I am hoping that simply replacing this might restore functionality. Are there other components that are likely to have sustained damage and should be considered for replacement? Additionally, I had two digital expansion modules connected, which now show obvious damage around the 24V input area on the PCB. I will provide a picture for reference. Can I get information on the six components located at the 24V input zone? Also, does [company_name] allow customers to purchase the motherboard PCB separately?

It is unlikely that the device can be repaired, as most parts are probably damaged beyond recovery. Replacement circuit boards are not sold individually, and it would be cost-prohibitive for [company_name] to offer and manage such options. The expense of individual boards would be nearly the same as purchasing an entirely new product. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user caused severe electrical damage to a [product_name] and connected expansion modules by applying incorrect voltage. The user requests advice on possible repairs and information about damaged components, specifically seeking replacement options for internal parts and PCBs. The replies make clear that individual replacement boards are not available and that extensive damage likely makes repair impractical.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to identify all damaged components, replace any discrete damaged parts, or acquire replacement PCBs to fix the affected hardware.
